fix or task.instructions: The state is one GitHub issue of the Imperial Conquest 2 build, a C# remake of a strategy game with a Godot UI: its title, then its body (a bug report or a review follow-up). Choose how the defect is fixed (docs/build-process.md §4.10). A fix stays within the files the issue names and changes no rule's outcome: it corrects a message, a guard, a rejection, a parser, a view, a dialog, a check scene, a test, a save path or a data file's provenance. It changes no ruleset key, no tests/fixtures/corpus.json value, no seeded measurement and no CLI golden line outside the bug's own reproduction. A task is needed when the fix alters what a rule computes, a gameplay constant, a battle resolver's result or an AI decision, however small, or needs files the issue does not name, its own Owns list, a design decision, or new art, data or evidence.

criteria.fix: The change stays in the named files and changes no rule's outcome: wording, a missing confirmation prompt, a dialog or view that composes the existing orders, a stale check or test, a parser or validation, a provenance string.
criteria.task: The change alters a rule, a constant, a guard that changes what an order does, a resolver or AI outcome, re-baselines seeded or golden values beyond the reproduction, spans files the issue does not name, or needs a decision, art or evidence first.

playability.instructions: The state is one GitHub issue of the Imperial Conquest 2 build: its title, then its body. Until the v0.5.0 tag the build sorts every bug and follow-up by the playability gate (docs/build-process.md §4.8). A normal game is a human seat, or hotseat seats, in a shipped scenario under either shipped preset, played through the Godot app's menus, toolbars, map clicks and dialogs, from New Game or a Load, to the scenario's victory condition or the seat's fall; the CLI, an imported original save, a custom world and a soak run are not normal games. Choose release:v0.5.0 when the issue breaks play (a crash, an AI stall, a save that will not load, an order that can never succeed) or fails one of three tests: (1) an order the original has cannot be issued in the Godot app, or is refused, ignored or clamped to no effect where the original carries it out (an order that works but looks different, a gap in the CLI only, or a missing keyboard shortcut does not count); (2) after an order, an end of turn or an AI phase, a player using only the Godot app cannot tell whether the order took effect, why it was refused, or what changed, or a figure on a panel is wrong for the rule the engine applies (a difference of wording or format, a missing flavour text, the news log's layout, or a fact the original also hides does not count); (3) under either preset a human seat playing sensibly cannot win, or loses or is stopped for a reason the original does not have (a constant or formula that differs but whose effect stays inside normal play does not count). Also choose release:v0.5.0, whatever the tests say, when the body records the user's decision to put the issue in the v0.5.0 gate, or says the issue blocks a task or fix that is in the v0.5.0 gate (a 'Blocks: T<nn>' line together with the gate). Choose post-v0.5.0 otherwise: cosmetic differences, wording, message order, missing guards that only let the player do more than the original allows, CLI-only gaps, internal code quality, documentation.

criteria.release:v0.5.0: It breaks play, or fails test 1, 2 or 3 in a normal game played through the Godot app, or the body records the user's decision to put it in the gate, or it blocks a task or fix in the v0.5.0 gate.
criteria.post-v0.5.0: It fails none of the three tests: cosmetic, wording or format, message order, a guard the original has that the clone lacks without stopping play, a CLI-only or internal issue, or documentation.
